question: The Looney Tunes comedy Coyote vs. Acme, starring Wile E. Coyote, finally reached US cinemas in August 2026, years after it was finished. Why had Warner Bros. shelved the completed film in 2023?
alternative_answers: To write it off for tax purposes
A tax deduction was worth more than releasing it
Cheaper to bury it than release it
source_excerpt: Warner Bros. announced it would not release the finished film because parent company Warner Bros. Discovery preferred to claim a tax loss of about $30 million.

topicality.rationale: Hinges on the August 2026 release of a long-shelved film, a seasonal talking point.

extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms the tax-loss rationale (about $30M) for shelving in Nov 2023 and the Aug 28, 2026 US release via Ketchup Entertainment.

explanation: Warner Bros. Discovery had a finished, well-tested film, but in November 2023 it decided to shelve it and write it off for a tax benefit of around 30 million dollars. Releasing it would have cost more in marketing than the studio expected to earn. Filmmakers and fans protested loudly, and in March 2025 the independent distributor Ketchup Entertainment bought the film for about 50 million dollars. That is how Wile E. Coyote's lawsuit against Acme finally reached cinemas in August 2026.

question: Practical Magic 2 brought the witch sisters Sally and Gillian Owens back to cinemas in 2026, 28 years after the original. Sandra Bullock returned as Sally. Which Australian star returned as Gillian?
source_excerpt: Practical Magic 2, starring Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman, is set to debut on Sept. 18, 2026.

extra.why_interesting: A casual fan half-remembers the 1998 witch film; the sequel gives them a quick, satisfying win.

topicality.rationale: A big sequel release that stays in conversation for a season.

extra.verification_notes: Practical Magic 2 was released in September 2026 with Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman reprising Sally and Gillian; no contradicting developments found (https://au.variety.com/2025/film/news/practical-magic-2-release-date-nicole-kidman-sandra-bullock-22304).

explanation: Kidman and Bullock first played the Owens sisters in 1998. Stockard Channing and Dianne Wiest also came back as their eccentric aunts.

question: The fifth Avengers film, set for a December 2026 release, brings Robert Downey Junior back to Marvel, but not as Iron Man. Which metal-masked Fantastic Four villain does he play?
source_excerpt: Robert Downey Jr. is confirmed as Doctor Doom; Avengers: Doomsday release date is December 18, 2026.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume Marvel's most famous hero is coming back as Tony Stark. Instead he plays the franchise's biggest villain.

topicality.rationale: A major upcoming Marvel tentpole; the casting stays a talking point for about a year.

extra.verification_notes: Downey Jr. is confirmed as Doctor Doom in Avengers: Doomsday, dated Dec 18, 2026, with no later delay found (https://www.dexerto.com/tv-movies/avengers-doomsday-release-date-cast-plot-more-1949725).

explanation: Downey plays Victor von Doom, which explains the film's title, Avengers: Doomsday. It is a full reversal for the actor who launched the whole Marvel film universe as its hero.

question: In Christopher Nolan's 2026 epic The Odyssey, Zendaya plays the Greek goddess who watches over the hero on his long voyage home. Which goddess?
source_excerpt: Zendaya plays Athena, the goddess who protects Odysseus on his journey.

extra.why_interesting: Players who never read Homer still know the Greek gods. They have to recall which goddess watches over Odysseus.

topicality.rationale: A major Nolan film of 2026 that stays culturally relevant for about a year.

extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms Zendaya plays Athena (plus a Trojan priestess of Athena) in Nolan's The Odyssey; no contradicting or newer information found.

explanation: In Homer's poem, Athena, goddess of wisdom, is Odysseus's great divine ally. In the film's cast, Tom Holland plays his son Telemachus and Anne Hathaway plays his wife Penelope.

question: Netflix's 2026 season Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story revisits the 1892 axe murders that inspired a grim children's skipping rhyme. What was the verdict at Lizzie Borden's real trial in 1893?
source_excerpt: Lizzie Borden was acquitted of the murders of her father, Andrew, and her stepmother, Abby. The jury reached its decision on June 20, 1893.

extra.why_interesting: The playground rhyme treats Lizzie as a proven murderer, so players assume she was convicted. In reality the jury acquitted her.

topicality.rationale: The Netflix season is only a hook; the question is history, but it is fresher while the show is airing.

extra.verification_notes: Lizzie Borden was acquitted at her June 1893 trial; the Netflix season and skipping rhyme details in the question also check out (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lizzie_Borden).

explanation: The jury acquitted her and the murders were never officially solved. The rhyme gets other details wrong too: the victim was her stepmother, and there were far fewer than forty whacks.

question: Ted Lasso returned for a fourth season in August 2026. Long before the series, Jason Sudeikis first played the clueless American coach in TV adverts promoting US coverage of which football league?
source_excerpt: Ted Lasso season four will make its global debut on Wednesday, August 5, with one episode, followed by new episodes every Wednesday through October 7.

extra.why_interesting: Players think of Ted Lasso as an original prestige comedy. It actually began as a joke character in sports-channel ads.

topicality.rationale: The season 4 return gives the trivia a seasonal hook.

extra.verification_notes: Season 4 premiered Aug 5, 2026 per MacTech; the 2013 NBC Sports promos for Premier League coverage are from prior knowledge, not re-checked by search.

explanation: NBC Sports made the promos in 2013 to sell English football to Americans. The fish-out-of-water joke later grew into a hit series.

question: In the 1970s, Dolly Parton refused to let the biggest rock and roll star in the world record her song 'I Will Always Love You', because his manager demanded half of her publishing rights. Who was the star?
source_excerpt: Presley's manager, Colonel Tom Parker, told her that the songwriter would be expected to sign over half of the publishing rights

extra.why_interesting: Players know only the Dolly and Whitney versions. Learning that the biggest star in the world was turned down is a real surprise.

topicality.rationale: Historical music trivia with no news hook.

extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms Elvis wanted to record the song in the 1970s and Colonel Parker demanded half the publishing, so Parton refused.

explanation: Parton kept the rights, and that decision paid off hugely when Whitney Houston's 1992 version spent fourteen weeks at number one in America.

question: When the total solar eclipse of August 2026 swept across Iceland and Spain, streams of Bonnie Tyler's 'Total Eclipse of the Heart' jumped worldwide. Its songwriter originally wrote it as a love song about which creatures?
source_excerpt: actually wrote that to be a vampire love song... Its original title was 'Vampires in Love'

extra.why_interesting: The song sounds like a straightforward heartbreak ballad. It was actually written for a vampire musical, which makes the lyrics about darkness feel very different.

topicality.rationale: The eclipse streaming spike is a short-lived news hook.

extra.verification_notes: Steinman said he wrote the song as a vampire love song, originally titled 'Vampires in Love'; the eclipse framing is accurate (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_Eclipse_of_the_Heart).

explanation: Jim Steinman first called it 'Vampires in Love' and meant it for a Nosferatu stage musical. That explains all the lines about darkness and the night.

question: When Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone was first published in Britain in June 1997, roughly how many hardback copies were in its first print run?
source_excerpt: one of 500 first edition, first impression hardcovers

extra.why_interesting: Knowing it became a global phenomenon, players assume a big launch. The real first printing was tiny.

topicality.rationale: Publishing history from 1997 with no current news hook.

extra.verification_notes: Multiple auction houses and dealers cite a first print run of 500 hardcovers, such as Lyon & Turnbull; no newer development contradicts this, though the split between library and retail copies varies by source.

explanation: Only about 500 hardbacks were printed, and most of them went to libraries. Those first editions are now among the most valuable modern books in the world.

question: Super Mario is the most famous plumber in pop culture, but he did not start out fixing pipes. In his 1981 arcade debut, Donkey Kong, what was his job?
source_excerpt: labeled a carpenter at first and was later identified as a plumber

extra.why_interesting: Everyone 'knows' Mario is a plumber, since it's his whole identity. Few realise his first job was different. A player can reason it out: he climbs girders on a building site to rescue someone from a giant ape, so the construction trade fits.

topicality.rationale: Video game history trivia about 1981; not tied to any current news.

extra.verification_notes: Jumpman (later Mario) was a carpenter in the 1981 Donkey Kong; he became a plumber later with Mario Bros. (https://StrategyWiki.org/wiki/Donkey_Kong).

explanation: In Donkey Kong he was a carpenter called Jumpman, climbing girders on a building site. He only became a plumber in 1983's Mario Bros., which takes place in the sewers, and by then he had been named after the landlord of Nintendo's American warehouse.
